description: Curated SecHub Resources SC4S pack for HashiCorp Vault audit device JSON records relayed as one JSON object per line, with fixture-backed request, response, error response, auth, token lifecycle, secret, namespace, policy, policy-denied, and audit-device administration families.

normalized_fields.vault_client_id: Vault request.client_id when present; client identifier context from audit schema

normalized_fields.vault_token_lifecycle: Derived token lifecycle helper for auth/token create, renew, lookup, and revoke paths; fixture-backed only for token creation response context
normalized_fields.vault_token_type: Vault auth.token_type from response/auth context when present
normalized_fields.vault_token_ttl: Vault response.auth.lease_duration for token lifecycle response context
normalized_fields.vault_token_renewable: Vault response.auth.renewable flag for token lifecycle response context
normalized_fields.vault_token_policies: Vault response.auth.policies list for token lifecycle response context
normalized_fields.vault_token_orphan: Vault response.auth.orphan flag for token lifecycle response context

pack_variants.label: Vault audit JSON relay
pack_variants.description: Default Vault audit JSON entries preserving request/response type, request ID, operation, path, actor, remote address, namespace/mount context, audit-device administration path context, token lifecycle response context, policy decision/override context, and error/status context including fixture-backed error and policy-denied responses.
known_limitations: No live Vault audit relay replay/read-back captured.
Only default JSON audit entries are fixture-backed; jsonx, prefix, log_raw=true, and exact syslog envelopes are out of scope.

Request, response, error response, auth, token lifecycle, secret, namespace/mount-context, audit-device administration, policy/system-change, and policy-denied families are fixture-backed; endpoint-specific data shapes, exact token lifecycle side effects, and exact audit-device option effects remain future coverage.
pack_variants.event_boundary: One Vault audit JSON object per line. File/socket/collector relays should split records before SC4S; the fixture send helper wraps each JSON line as one TCP syslog message for the dedicated listener.
pack_variants.events_per_file_or_message: Fixture file contains multiple records, but each line is one event; after relay wrapping, each TCP/syslog message carries one JSON audit object.
pack_variants.uniqueness_or_multiline: Audit records are expected to be single-line JSON objects, not multiline payloads. Fixture markers are per-event JSON fields and each declared marker appears exactly once.
pack_variants.field_delimiting_or_escaping: JSON field names and values use standard JSON escaping; no CSV or key=value delimiter is assumed. jsonx, custom prefix, and log_raw=true payload variants remain out of scope until exact source evidence is added.
pack_variants.timestamp_timezone: Primary event time is the JSON time field, expected as ISO-8601/RFC3339 with timezone in the fixture-backed scope. Syslog wrapper/header timestamps are relay metadata and do not replace the Vault source time without replay/read-back evidence.

cribl.notes: Use only after sampling the local Vault audit feed. Do not drop time, type, request.id, request.operation, request.path, auth/entity context, remote address, error, or raw JSON by default.

vector.notes: Vector support is recorded as a conservative sources/transforms/sinks mapping only: native syslog listener or relay-to-syslog path; preserve the pack sourcetype/source routing and validate listener framing locally. No Vector config artifact is generated by this pack yet.

Only default JSON audit entries are covered; jsonx, prefixes, raw-secret logging, exact syslog envelopes, additional enterprise namespace variants, exact token lifecycle side effects, exact audit-device option effects, complete policy-engine semantics, and endpoint-specific data shapes remain future coverage.
